page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with a high memory-to-vCPU allocation. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC core running at 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). It includes 16 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, 32 MB of L3 cache, and 100 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration hardware is not included, with GPU count standing at zero.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial single-thread processing capabilities alongside predictable multi-core scaling limitations. In single-core tests, the AMD processor performs exceptionally well, achieving top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution and strong scores in Geekbench single-core, text processing, and single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, overall throughput metrics such as Geekbench multi-core, PassMark CPU, Clang compilation, and ray tracing rank in the lower quartile due to the two-vCPU ceiling. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks operates at moderate speeds of roughly 74 to 76 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides strong cost efficiency for footprints requiring high memory capacity without the overhead of unused compute cores. Because it features dedicated vCPUs and bundled NVMe storage, performance remains deterministic without hypervisor contention. The server is well aligned for lightweight in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, background compression workers, and single-threaded or memory-intensive microservices.
description: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is a memory-weighted virtual machine within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single AMD EPYC physical core operating at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 16 GB of RAM, equating to an 8 GB per vCPU distribution, alongside 100 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, demonstrated by top-tier single-core stress-ng throughput and solid compression speeds, contrasted with lower multi-core aggregate metrics expected from a dual-vCPU ceiling. Uncached memory read and write bandwidth remain consistent at mid-range operational tiers. This resource composition offers an efficient deployment target for memory-bound applications that do not require wide core scaling, such as lightweight in-memory data structures, caching layers, low-traffic relational databases, and single-threaded batch processing services.
